title: Single-cut coding and reveal timing
summary: Exact small-source codebook enumeration separates a late queried coordinate from an early relevance cue. The isolated four-bit first cut has error 3/16; the isolated one-bit three-coordinate child has error 1/4.
limitations: One memory boundary in the timing comparison; it does not establish the two-stage chain optimum.

title: Four-bit parent/child compatibility
summary: Three parent bits suffice and are necessary to attain the isolated child optimum of 25%. The earlier two-bit certificate supplies only a conservative 49/192 lower bound.
limitations: The separate exact-chain computation sharpens this bound to 9/32; do not treat the conservative certificate as the optimum.

title: Scaling, leave-one-out and independent proof checks
summary: Local information arguments allow joint encoding across blocks: exact child-optimal error needs 3k parent bits; 2k parent bits force error above 1/4 + 1/512. Independent finite checks audit the proof ingredients.
limitations: Local derivation with external review open; do not multiply the one-block 1/32 excess across arbitrary joint encodings.

title: Exact four-bit chain optimum
summary: Complete enumeration of 171,798,901 four-cell partitions establishes exact error 9/32; 128 partitions attain it. The saved witness is independently graded.
limitations: Routine checks verify the search source, count and witness; they do not repeat the full exhaustive search.

title: Two-block witness and asymptotic threshold
summary: The two-block witness attains 283/1024 error on all 6,144 outcomes. A rational channel gives the earlier asymptotic upper bound 101/384; the threshold for approaching 1/4 is about 2.5488 parent bits per block.
limitations: The two-block optimum is not claimed. Later decoder-complete and all-rate results strengthen the earlier asymptotic bound.

title: Decoder-complete rate-two frontier
summary: All 1,679,616 legal final tables are covered. The limiting error at two parent bits per block is strictly between 0.2618989799 and 0.2618989801; the lower bound holds at every finite block count.
limitations: Uniform finite bit model; no model trials or practical-agent result. External correctness and priority review remain open.

title: Explicit three-block witness
summary: 40,529 errors on all 147,456 outcomes, versus 40,992 for the earlier concatenation, at six parent bits and one child bit.
limitations: Achievable construction, not a finite optimum. C69 later improves the witness to 40,514 without rewriting this certificate.

title: Restricted three-block converse
summary: The restricted final-decoder family has lower bound 40,072/147,456 and the historical 40,529 upper witness.
limitations: This converse alone assumes final predictions independent of late coordinate J; later converse packages extend coverage.

title: Complementary three-block converse
summary: All 256 complementary tables per block are covered, including J-dependent predictions; the lower bound remains 40,072/147,456.
limitations: Noncomplementary endpoints are outside this certificate; C63 covers them.

title: Unrestricted three-block converse
summary: An oracle gate and 46,492 near mixed cases cover all final decoders, establishing lower bound 40,072/147,456.
limitations: The historical upper witness is 40,529; C69 tightens it to 40,514. Exact finite optimality remains open.

title: Parent-rate support spectrum
summary: Eight rational-rate intervals and an analytic unsigned support transition near 0.620690001029 bits per block are checked.
limitations: The unrestricted curve between these checks was open at this milestone; C67 later resolves it.

title: Balanced-source complementary completion
summary: Complementary final endpoints suffice at every block count and parent capacity under the balanced-source average-error contract. Checks cover 9,216 branch cases and 3,686,400 whole-code routes.
limitations: A biased-source counterexample and individual harms delimit the result; the numerical frontier is unchanged.

title: Full unrestricted asymptotic rate curve
summary: Forty-eight exact polynomial comparisons certify the unrestricted curve at every parent rate; error reaches the 1/4 floor near 2.548795 bits per block.
limitations: Uniform source and stated delayed-query law; no efficient finite near-curve code or natural-workflow result follows.

title: Finite trellis construction
summary: An exact 16-state encoder has 867,837 errors on 3,145,728 four-block outcomes, versus pair-product 869,376, with eight parent bits and one child bit. Public labels occupy 96 packed bytes.
limitations: Smaller cycles lose; the existing three-block product wins at common lengths 12n. Longer-cycle optimality is open.

title: Conditional six-block construction
summary: 331,857,648 errors on 1,207,959,552 outcomes at 12 parent bits and one child bit, improving a refined product. The three-block bracket tightens to [40,072,40,514]/147,456.
limitations: Small finite gain; no final six-block optimum or locality certificate. Public payload is 120 bytes.

title: Query-prior allocation and timing
summary: Known 25%/75% class priors have limiting error near 25.718661%; unknown-prior minimax retains the uniform limit. An early actual class cue reaches 25% using 3n bits within the same 4n cap.
limitations: Source-independent class priors only. Early realized side information changes the timing contract; it is not merely a prior.

title: Hard-cap entropy construction
summary: A flagged 2k-bit parent and one-bit child have risk at most 27.198892% at k=12,288 under the retained rational schedule. The default family tends to about 27.075301%; public tables use 10 packed bytes.
limitations: Large-population values are conservative bounds, not enumerated exact averages. Four smaller lengths lose to stronger controls.

title: Coordinated equal-loss response construction
summary: The fixed-eight code has risk at most 27.080384% at k=12,288 with the same instance caps. Its limit is about 26.929308%; a separate growing-group family tends to 26.782918%.
limitations: Public fixed data increase to 1,288 packed bytes. Smaller losses remain; both limits exceed C67 and no practical-agent gain follows.

title: Deterministic convergence construction
summary: An implemented polynomial family at exactly 2k parent bits and one child bit converges to the C67 rate-two optimum at every integer length.
limitations: Useful finite convergence is unresolved: small codes lose to stronger controls and conservative near-limit group sizes are enormous. Large books were not built.

title: Loss-weighted overflow and allocation bounds
summary: The unchanged C72 actors yield error at most 27.450867% at 768 blocks and 27.064671% at 12,288. Exact integer allocation minimizes five outward bounds; tables remain 1,288 bytes.
limitations: Certificate minimization is not actual-risk or global code optimality. Three smaller lengths lose; all 384 unsuccessful quantizer starts are retained.

title: Exact-priced larger-group construction
summary: At k=12,288 error is at most 27.047565% with the same 2k-bit parent and one-bit child. All ten starts and 41,943,040 source assignments retain independent minimum checks.
limitations: The small gain costs 94,754 public bytes including planning weights and 11-19 second local encodes. A separate actual-limit family reaches about 26.901709%, worse than growing C72. No finite-selector limit, global optimum or agent gain is established.

limitations: Configurations are not independent model trials. Record slots and serialized bytes are distinct units; no superiority over deployed harnesses.
